thread.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Gets Lift From Advanced Chips | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Gets Lift From Advanced Chips | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) on Thursday reported in-line earnings on better-than-expected sales for the third quarter, but disappointed with its sales guidance for the current quarter. TSMC stock fell along with the broader market.
X The chip foundry, known as TSMC, earned 56 cents per U.S. share in the September quarter, matching Wall Street's target. It generated sales of $8.49 billion, topping the consensus estimate of $8.4 billion. On a year-over-year basis, earnings slipped 3%, but sales rose 2%. In local currency, earnings dipped 1% and sales rose 3%.
For the current quarter, Taiwan Semiconductor expects sales of $9.4 billion, based on the midpoint of its guidance. Wall Street was modeling $9.8 billion. TSMC did not give an estimate for earnings per share, but analysts were targeting 70 cents.
TSMC's U.S. stock dropped 2.7% to 38.52 on the stock market today . It has been consolidating for 38 weeks with a buy point of 46.67. But shares are trading well below their 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

Fast Ramp Of 7-Nanometer Chips "Our third-quarter business benefited from new product launches using TSMC 7-nanometer technology," Chief Financial Officer Lora Ho said in a news release . "Moving into fourth quarter 2018, we anticipate our business will continue to benefit from the strong demand for our 7-nanometer technology."
Circuit widths on chips are measured in nanometers, which are one-billionth of a meter.
In the third quarter, 7-nanometer chips accounted for 11% of TSMC's total wafer revenue. It was the first quarter that TSMC generated revenue from the smaller-scale chips. Advanced technologies, defined as chips with 28 nanometer or smaller nodes, accounted for 61% of total wafer revenue last quarter, the company said.
Susquehanna Financial Group analyst Mehdi Hosseini said 7-nanometer chips could exceed 20% of TSMC's wafer revenue in the fourth quarter. The growth will be driven by high-end smartphones such as the Apple iPhone XS, he said in a note to clients.
